profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer at Extron
profile.summary: As a software engineer and cloud architect, I collaborate with stakeholders and engineering teams to build, evolve, and maintain software systems; and I believe that building a software system is a team sport where great teams practice excellence in communication, education, and reflection as part of great engineering.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
Our team at Extron is responsible for developing cloud software in support of Extron's AV and control products for enterprise customers. We deliver network and device management solutions for Extron's AV and control products.

While I've been with Extron, I've worked on cloud and system architecture for several products. As our program's lead cloud architect, I collaborate with product owners, engineering teams, and vendors to design, plan, prototype, and deliver system infrastructure and services running in the AWS public cloud.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Our team at NetIQ was responsible for a wide range of application management modules that integrate with NetIQ's AppManager product, a distributed service-oriented system. AppManager's VoIP and unified communications system management products provide customers with tools for network infrastructure assessment, cross-vendor system monitoring, and VoIP quality of service reporting.

While I was with NetIQ, I worked on a number of AppManager module products, including modules to monitor Avaya and Nortel Unified Communications, Cisco Unified Communications, Microsoft Lync Server, Microsoft SQL Server, Microsoft SharePoint Server, Network Performance, SNMP, VoIP Quality of Service, and Website Performance. As a senior software engineer, I collaborated with product owners and other engineering team members to design, plan, deliver, and maintain Appmanager modules and components authored in C/C++, C#, and PowerShell.

An example product I worked on was AppManager's SIP server module QoS collector which receives and processes QoS reports from SIP servers and creates a database of call quality information derived from these reports. This RFC-6035 compliant SIP QoS collector includes a C/C++ SIP stack to receive reports and store them in a SQL Server database for reporting.

company.name: NetIQ and Attachmate Corporations now Micro Focus International

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Our team in Varian’s Scientific Instruments business was responsible for automated dissolution testing products for pharmaceutical R&D and quality control laboratories. These systems provide software support for experimental method management, system configuration, data security, record retention, and auditing required for compliance with the FDA's 21 CFR Part 11 rules for electronic submissions.

As a software design engineer, I collaborated with research scientists, product owners, and other engineering team members to design, plan, deliver, and support automated dissolution testing products utilizing a common data model, SQL Server database, and a component-based design implemented in ATL/COM.

An example product I worked on was the Galaxie LC-Dissolution software, a client-server system which integrated remote Delphi-based GUIs and an ATL/COM-based middle-tier with the existing Galaxie chromatography data system.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Our team at Com-Net Ericsson (and then M/A-COM) was responsible for network and device management products that support the company's radio systems. These products were designed as three-tiered systems, and implemented in C/C++ and C# for Windows; they interacted with managed equipment using network protocols, and stored data using SQL Server databases.

As both a contributing and lead software engineer, I collaborated with product owners and other engineering team members to design, plan, deliver, and support management systems for the EDACS and APCO-P25 radio systems.

An example product I worked on was the network key management server for the APCO-P25 radio system which provided secure, network-wide, encryption key generation, management, and over-the-air key distribution to the radio system. The server interacted with radios using TCP/IP through a mixed middle-tier of object-oriented C/C++ and C#. The system's configuration, operational, and key data are stored in a SQL Server database.

company.name: Com-Net Ericsson and M/A-COM Inc. now Harris Corporation

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Norfolk City County, Virginia, United States
positions.description:
Our team at NASA LaRC's Air Traffic Operations Lab worked on the Advanced Air Transportation Technologies project. This project's medium-fidelity simulation consisted of multiple single-pilot stations using networked simulators running simulation components in a CORBA environment, and providing OpenGL-based GUIs to researchers and subjects using a cross-platform C and C++ code-base.

As the lead engineer for several of the project's integration and development efforts, I collaborated with research scientists and other engineering team members to design, plan, deliver, and support simulation and data collection components.
